title: The Blue Tsunami Swept Doctors and Scientists Into Office
gist: The 314 Action Fund spent over $30M this midterm cycle, and 14 of its 17 House candidates won (9 flips), along with doctor/scientist winners such as El-Sayed, Andrews and Acton. Experts link the wave of science candidates to the Trump administration's hostility to expertise, lab defunding and RFK Jr.'s MAHA agenda, and call it a 'health care election'.

insights.claim: 314 Action Fund spent more than $30 million this cycle, including $3.6 million for Annie Andrews' South Carolina Senate race and $3 million for Amy Acton's Ohio governor campaign.
insights.speaker: Shaughnessy Naughton
insights.so_what: Shows how much single-issue PAC money went into health and science candidates.

insights.claim: 314 Action's success rate for congressional candidates topped 80%, with 14 of its 17 House candidates winning and nine seats flipped from Republican to Democrat.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Points to a Congress with more members who have technical backgrounds and favor science funding.
insights.quote: 14 of 17 of its candidates in the US House of Representatives winning their races

insights.claim: Naughton says the midterms turned out to be a health care election.
insights.speaker: Shaughnessy Naughton
insights.so_what: Health care policy is likely to dominate the new Congress's agenda.
insights.quote: It did turn out to be a health care election

insights.claim: Brookings' health policy director notes that what is unusual is not that scientists and health workers sit in Congress, but how many arrived in a single wave.
insights.speaker: Richard Frank
insights.so_what: A wave of this size could shift how committees handle science and health policy.
insights.quote: is just how many came in one wave

insights.claim: Frank attributes the surge in science candidates directly to the Trump administration's hostility toward medical and technical expertise.
insights.speaker: Richard Frank
insights.so_what: Political backlash could lead to restored science funding and oversight.

insights.claim: Rutgers' Eagleton Institute head attributes the trend to federal defunding of laboratories and scientific research, and to the pandemic's effect on health workers' political awareness.
insights.speaker: Kristoffer Shields
insights.so_what: Lab defunding is now a campaign issue, which could support reversals in research funding.
insights.locator: The rise of the science candidate

insights.claim: El-Sayed linked this summer's cyclospora outbreak to DOGE-directed mass layoffs at the FDA, saying 'We DOGE'd our whole service that keeps the lettuce safe.'
insights.speaker: Abdul El-Sayed
insights.so_what: Food safety capacity at the FDA is politically salient, so congressional oversight of cuts is likely.
insights.quote: We DOGE’d our whole service that keeps the lettuce safe

insights.claim: The author reads the election as partly a rejection of RFK Jr.'s MAHA movement and its medical misinformation, including anti-vaccine sentiment.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Pressure on HHS leadership and vaccine policy may matter for vaccine makers.
insights.locator: That so many of these politicians

insights.claim: Senator-elect Annie Andrews calls RFK Jr. her 'archnemesis' and has promised to hold him accountable.
insights.speaker: Annie Andrews
insights.so_what: Expect aggressive Senate oversight of HHS.
insights.locator: Shields sees the straightforward communication style

insights.claim: 314 Action launched its Guardians of Public Health initiative in 2025 to recruit health care experts to run against RFK Jr.'s HHS agenda, and is starting its next recruitment round this month.
insights.speaker: Shaughnessy Naughton
insights.so_what: The pipeline of science candidates is set to keep going into future cycles.

insights.claim: Microbiologist Jasmine Clark, first backed by 314 Action for the Georgia state house in 2018, is moving up to Congress, an example of a multi-year farm-team strategy.
insights.speaker: Shaughnessy Naughton
insights.so_what: Down-ballot investment has proven to pay off at the federal level.

insights.claim: 314 Action stopped accepting funding tied to AIPAC after scrutiny in 2024, and backed candidates critical of the Israeli government, such as El-Sayed.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: A shift in Democratic coalition politics on Israel.
